report.summary: Reviewed the three supplied files against the planned Cycle 23 guided first-use panel. The plan can reuse the CLI validator and cannot by itself inflate human-first-use counts, because summarizeFirstUseSessions counts only human_first_use sessions and requires consent, unfamiliar and external flags. However, the proposed panel integrates with lib/first-use-trial.ts, whose schema (first-use-local-v1, T01–T05, independent/with_help outcomes) does not match the v1 session schema (persona-scoped TASKS ids, completed/blocked/abandoned, helpCount, consent). The plan also does not say how the in-memory trial clock ties to the wall-clock startedAt/endedAt needed by the v1 validator. The validator allows a human_first_use session even when an operator or automation ran it, and a participant/repeated code can carry attestations (consent, unfamiliar, external) that the CLI does not check. This means the clean human aggregate depends on operator discipline, not on enforced input. There is no source showing a shared validator module yet, so the 'browser-safe' extraction is unverifiable and its required failure modes (Node-free imports, identical error codes, unchanged aggregation) are not covered. Findings below concern measurable claim, clock, privacy and context boundaries in the plan.

findings.title: Validator accepts human_first_use sessions without a source/operator field, so an operator-walkthrough run can be self-attested into the 'human' aggregate
findings.evidence: Line 42 gates human_first_use only on consent.status==='granted', unfamiliarWithProject and externalParticipant. There is no field that records who ran the session or whether automation issued the inputs. Line 28 states the validator 'cannot authenticate a person or prove a session occurred'. Line 52 rejects only zero-duration completions, so automation that generates distinct timestamps, a granted consent.recordedAt before start, and p-xxxxxxxx passes. lib/first-use-trial.ts line 5 has operator values 'developer'/'automation', and line 51 exports operatorTypeSelfDeclared:true, but line 52 never maps those onto the v1 mode, and the plan adds no rule to do so. A record can still be written as human_first_use and counted at line 67-69.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): build a v1 object with mode:'human_first_use', consent:{status:'granted',recordedAt:'2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'}, startedAt 00:00:01, endedAt 00:01:00, three buyer tasks with distinct timestamps and completed/none, unfamiliarWithProject/externalParticipant true. validateFirstUseSession returns a clone and summarizeFirstUseSessions counts it in humanSessions and byPersona.completed. Nothing in the object says a real unfamiliar external human entered it.
findings.suggestion: In the shared validator, require human_first_use sessions to carry an explicit operator/attestation field, such as operatorType of real_human only, taken from the same enum as lib/first-use-trial.ts. Map developer/automation/unknown to a non-human mode or reject them. Keep summarizeFirstUseSessions unchanged otherwise and add the flag to the UI self-report. Also add a CLI acceptance check that a record from the automation root CUA run can never be written as human_first_use.

findings.title: Trial durations use a monotonic origin and have no wall-clock start/end. The plan does not define how the panel produces the v1 startedAt/endedAt/consent.recordedAt that the validator checks
findings.evidence: Lines 22-23 compute elapsed = Math.round(now - trial.monotonicOrigin), and line 28 stores only monotonicOrigin and lastMonotonic. startFirstUseTask (line 32) and finishFirstUseTask (line 42) store startedMs/endedMs as offsets, with no ISO timestamps. The v1 validator requires full ISO instants for startedAt, endedAt, consent.recordedAt and each task.startedAt/endedAt (lines 23-24, 37, 50) and enforces end>=start, span<=8h, consent.recordedAt<=start (line 40), tasks contiguous and within the session (line 51), and no zero-duration human completion (line 52). The panel must derive wall time from performance.now(), which the plan names as the clock. If it adds the trial's monotonic offsets to an ISO epoch string only at export, validators lines 38, 40, 51 and 52 are satisfied trivially, because the ISO dates are not the real performance-clock instants. Nothing pins trial.startedAt to the epoch used for monotonicOrigin, so the durations can be styled and still pass.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): if the plan stores startedAt = ISO(t0) and task times = ISO(t0 + attempt.startedMs), a reviewer cannot recover whether t0 was captured when createFirstUseTrial was called. If the export instead synthesizes evenly spaced timestamps, the CLI accepts them because it only checks ordering and bounds, never that the string form matches monotonicOrigin.
findings.suggestion: At createFirstUseTrial, capture Date.now() once together with monotonicOrigin and keep it as sessionStartedEpochMs. At consent capture, record consent.recordedAt from that same anchor. When exporting the v1 record, derive each ISO time from anchor + monotonic offset and also keep the raw monotonic offsets/elapsedMs in the v1 tasks (small optional field) so reviewers can detect a re-anchored clock. Document this mapping in the shared module.

findings.title: Panel source is T01–T05 and the outcomes differ from the CLI, so the plan's 'three existing TASKS' and 'exact existing v1 session JSON' are contradictory for the integrated surface
findings.evidence: FIRST_USE_TASKS at line 3 is ['T01'..'T05'], and TRIAL_ACTIONS at line 7 includes business actions such as submit_v1, simulate_payment and accept_local. The v1 validator uses persona-keyed ids, buyer:[create-requirements,interpret-evidence,request-revision] and technical_seller:[integrate-staging,submit-delivery,repair-and-retest], and requires exactly three tasks in order (line 43, line 47). TrialOutcome at line 6 is independent/with_help/not_completed/unavailable/stopped. The v1 OUTCOMES at line 9 are completed/blocked/abandoned. The plan says the panel records outcomes 'completed/abandoned' and a help counter, but the plan does not say whether the panel replaces lib/first-use-trial.ts or reuses it. If it reuses it, the trial export fails v1 validation; if it replaces it, the existing trial's tests and exported records stop matching and an outcome mapping must be specified.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a trial created by createFirstUseTrial exports operator and an events/attempts schema of first-use-local-v1 (lines 49-52). Passing that export to validateFirstUseSession fails with INVALID_SESSION_SCHEMA at line 16, because the keys differ from the list at line 30. A plan that claims both 'existing trial' and 'exact v1' must specify the mapping.
findings.suggestion: State the mapping in the plan: with_help -> completed with helpCount>0, not_completed -> blocked with a code, stopped -> abandoned, and unavailable either rejected or mapped to abandoned with code other. Either replace FIRST_USE_TASKS with the persona TASKS imported from the shared module and derive trial tasks/actions from it, or mark lib/first-use-trial.ts as the guest-lab surface (line 51 already says guest-lab) and keep the panel on the v1 schema. In both cases, derive TASKS from one module.

findings.title: Repeated-participant exclusion trusts a client-supplied participantCode. The plan's 'preserve anonymous coded participant' wording does not define how codes are generated or checked when the panel writes the file
findings.evidence: Line 32 accepts any /^p-[a-z0-9]{6,20}$/ code. Lines 68-69 exclude the second record with the same code. summarizeFirstUseSessions has no way to know which records it has seen, other than the directory it is given. A panel that lets the user type the code can duplicate one person across persona folders, or reuse another person's code to erase that person's second session. Line 19's unsafe filter is not applied to participantCode, but the regex excludes punctuation, so email-like codes cannot pass.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): two valid records with participantCode 'p-abcdef' and different sessionIds and modes human_first_use. summarizeFirstUseSessions accepts the first and increments excluded.repeated_participant for the second (lines 68-69). Nothing in the code or the plan ties a code to a person.
findings.suggestion: Keep the anonymous code but add optional duplicate detection that does not rely on the code: have the panel generate a random code once per session with crypto.getRandomValues and never expose it for editing, and document in the plan that the code is an opaque link token rather than an identity. Do not add any identity fields.

findings.title: Date.parse accepts non-ISO startedAt, and the plan needs the UI to produce the exact validator format
findings.evidence: createFirstUseTrial (line 27) accepts any value for which Date.parse returns finite, including e.g. 'March 3 2026'. The v1 validator requires the strict ·\d{3}Z form with toISOString() equality (lines 23-24). If the panel copies trial.startedAt, or an equivalent, into the v1 record, the UI can create records the CLI rejects. Separately, lib/first-use-trial.ts never applies the v1 `unsafe` text scan: operator and build are constrained by regex, and there are no free-text fields. That is fine, but the v1 note and help/task UI must run safe() with max 300 and unsafe regex on every optional note so the 'small optional notes' claim holds.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): create a trial with startedAt '2026-03-03 10:00:00' (passes line 27). Put the same string into a v1 session startedAt and call validateFirstUseSession: it throws INVALID_TIMESTAMP at line 24.
findings.suggestion: In createFirstUseTrial, replace !Number.isFinite(Date.parse(startedAt)) with the same strict regex + toISOString equality used at lines 23-24 of the record script, and route every note through safe(value, 300, false) in the shared module.

findings.title: The record command has no check that --output is outside the repo or absent. The plan claims 'no projectsource' but the CLI only checks the content regex
findings.evidence: Line 99 accepts any --output path with no containment check. Line 101 uses flag 'wx' so an existing file is never overwritten (the plan keeps this). Content is limited to the v1 keys, and note text is scanned by `unsafe` (lines 12, 19). So the record cannot embed source, but it can be written into a project directory, where it is a stray generated file that may be picked up later. Member email and credentials are blocked only by the regex: multiline/URL schemes beyond http(s) are not listed, and e.g. a raw access token format that does not match the sk-/bearer patterns would pass.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): `--input ok.json --output ./apps/web/session.json` succeeds if the file does not exist. A note like 'sk_live' plus a non-matching token format would be accepted, and the panel's export would place a session file under the site tree.
findings.suggestion: In the browser export, use a Blob download rather than a CLI --output path. In the CLI, add an optional --output-dir allowlist, or at least print the resolved path in the result. Extend the plan to say the panel's export goes through the shared safe() only and that no extra free-text field is ever added beyond note (max 300).

limitations: Only scripts/record-first-use-session.mjs, lib/first-use-trial.ts and the SKILL.md packet were available. The existing main compact workbench, the new shared validator module, the tests and docs were not supplied, so I cannot confirm whether the shared module exists, whether it is truly Node-free, or whether the CLI re-export keeps error codes and aggregation behavior identical.
No files were changed and no commands, tests, typecheck, build or browser checks were run. All findings are source-reading traces, and each reproduction is labeled unexecuted.
The award references (IBM Bob 2026 The Green Room, Gemini 2024 Best Overall Jayu) and the '0 real human results' claim could not be checked against official announcements from this packet.
JSX/timing behavior of the proposed UI panel (performance.now monotonicity across tab suspension, download flow, collapsed bilingual copy) is not in the packet, so I could not assess it.

The critique is limited to measurable plan items: source privacy, clock integrity, schema/context boundaries, claim boundaries and human aggregation. It does not review visual design or the current codebase beyond the two files supplied.
